newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX closes firm, riding high on strong dlr.
newsitem.headline: German DAX closes firm, riding high on strong dlr.

text.p: German share prices climbed higher in late session trading on Monday, extending the strong gains put on during the bourse session as investors continued to direct funds towards Germany.

By the end of afterhours trading the IBIS DAX index had jumped nearly one percent to 4,400.30 points, marking a strong gain from the close of bourse trading which left the DAX index up 1.24 percent 4,371.16.
While last week's record-breaking rally appeared fully intact, dealers noted the morning activity was slightly more subdued as investors were being a little cautious.
But by late afternoon and against the backdrop of a stubbornly strong dollar and no other lucrative investment opportunities, the German share market was flying high again.
"I cannot believe it myself," said a dealer, adding however that it would be unwise to speculate against this trend.

One of the main factors powering the market ahead is the strong U.S. dollar, trading around 1.8467 marks in late afternoon. A weaker mark is seen to benefit German exporters as it makes German goods cheaper abroad.
Looking ahead, analysts at Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG wrote "....we see the long-term upward trend on the bourse as remaining stable."
"Signs of interim technical corrections have strengthened recently but the corrections should be limited. Weak days therefore continue to be suited to appropriate portfolio increases."
Corporate earnings are rising amid low-inflation growth and historically low interest rates, while Germany's savers appear finally to have acknowledged equities as a viable investment, analysts said.

Chemical, engineering and carmaking stocks were among the favourites on Monday and sportswear maker Puma AG was a standout among rumours that Italian fashion giant Benetton might be considering taking over the group.
Both Puma and Benetton denied the talk.
Electrical giant Siemens AG rose nearly five percent to 130.45 marks, gaining from positive analysts' assessments in the wake of nine-month results published least week.
